title: Oscar and the Ghost
premise: Rafael Ravensworth, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent years laundering his own identity into something unremarkable, is living under witness protection after testifying against the Voss banking syndicate. When he finds the safe house listed on a real-estate site with interior photos — including one of him asleep on the couch — he realizes someone inside the protection program is selling him. His handler, Elena Marsh, may be his only ally or his executioner, and the syndicate's accountant, Ilse Brandt, is defecting with ledgers that could burn them all before an international summit in Vienna. Rafael must extract Ilse while deciding whether justice served by a compromised system is worth anything at all. In the end, Rafael trades his testimony and his clean new life to expose both the syndicate and the corrupt marshals protecting it, escaping with Elena and Ilse as fugitives who have finally stopped lying.
about_author: Marguerite Pemberton is a former compliance auditor who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose careful lives come apart, drawing on the quiet paranoia of financial crime work.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Bored in witness protection, he idly searches the safe house address and finds it for sale — with photos of the interior, including one of himself asleep. Panic replaces routine; he checks the go-bag, tests the window, calls no one. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing invisibility was always rented, never owned.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Rafael's POV: how a promising investigator became the man who noticed the Voss syndicate's ledgers, testified, and lost everything — wife, name, career. He remembers packing the go-bag the night his marriage ended. Emotional beat: grief dressed up as preparedness.

chapters.title: Handler
chapters.summary: Elena Marsh's POV. She reviews Rafael's file and notices the real-estate listing herself, hours after he does. She reports it up the chain and gets a suspiciously smooth reassurance. She begins quietly pulling access logs. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into suspicion of her own agency.

chapters.title: The Man Who Buys Houses
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A friendly estate agent arrives unannounced for a 'valuation,' asking questions that don't fit a sale. Rafael plays the bland witness but spots a surveillance van outside. That night he moves to a motel, leaving the house staged to look occupied. Emotional beat: the hunter's patience recognized from the prey's side.

chapters.title: Ilse Brandt Signs Nothing
chapters.summary: Vienna, Ilse's POV. The Voss syndicate's chief accountant prepares her defection, copying ledgers onto two drives she hides separately. Her contact inside the summit planning committee warns her the extraction window closes when the conference convenes. Emotional beat: cold courage of a woman who has already priced her own life.

chapters.title: Marsh's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. The access logs show the listing photos came from a marshal's inspection camera — someone inside the program. Her supervisor orders her to stand down and move Rafael anyway, to a location only three people know. Emotional beat: duty pulling one way, evidence pulling the other.

chapters.title: Two Drives
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Elena visits the motel, breaks protocol, and tells him about Ilse Brandt: if Rafael helps verify her ledgers, the program will relocate him abroad before the summit. He knows a defector carrying that much leverage is also perfect bait. He agrees anyway. Emotional beat: choosing risk over waiting to be found.

chapters.title: The Vanishing Act
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Her extraction escort never arrives; instead, two men claiming to be program security take her 'protective custody.' She palms one drive into a hotel planter and goes with them, memorizing the route. Emotional beat: terror managed like arithmetic.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. She traces the fake security team to a front company owned by a Voss lieutenant — and finds a second signature on the transfer order: her own supervisor. She photographs everything and says nothing. Emotional beat: the loneliness of knowing your institution is the crime scene.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in the Prater
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, now in Vienna on a forged passport Elena shouldn't have been able to get. He retrieves Ilse's abandoned drive from the planter minutes before a sweep team does, and glimpses the man from the valuation visit. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by the certainty he's being allowed to run.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Say
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating short sections. Rafael decrypts the first drive: payments routed through the protection program itself — witnesses sold, some killed. Ilse, captive in a safe flat, stalls her interrogators by offering the second drive's location. Emotional beat: the sick clarity that survival has a market price.

chapters.title: The Summit Convenes
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Delegations arrive in Vienna; the syndicate needs Ilse silenced and the ledgers discredited before a financial-transparency vote. Elena is assigned to the program's summit liaison desk — inside the machine she's trying to expose. Emotional beat: wearing the enemy's badge.

chapters.title: Negotiation with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Rafael contacts Ilse's captors posing as a broker who can deliver the second drive — for a face-to-face with her. They agree, too easily. He recognizes the trap's shape but walks in anyway, because Ilse is the only witness who can corroborate his testimony. Emotional beat: love of justice outweighing self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Room Where It Happens
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The meeting: Rafael, the Voss lieutenant, and a marshal she recognizes from her own aborted extraction. Guns appear; Rafael's cover story holds just long enough for Ilse to slip him the room's layout. A smoke alarm — Elena, off-book — breaks it open. Emotional beat: strangers trusting each other faster than their institutions ever did.

chapters.title: Running on Empty
chapters.summary: Rafael and Ilse's POV, interleaved flight through Vienna: U-Bahn, rooftops, a night market. Ilse reveals the second drive names Elena's supervisor as the seller of witnesses — and hints there's a third name Rafael won't expect. Emotional beat: two survivors becoming allies, then something like friends.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The third name is his late wife — alive, relocated years ago under the same program, her safety used as leverage over him all along. He rages at Elena, who admits she knew. Emotional beat: betrayal inside betrayal; the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Marsh Breaks
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Cornered between her oath and her conscience, she copies the program's internal files and sends them to Rafael and a journalist, knowing it ends her career and possibly her life. Her supervisor begins closing the net. Emotional beat: duty redefined — not obedience, but the thing you refuse to become.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Climax part one, Rafael's POV. The syndicate offers a trade: Ilse and the drives for his ex-wife's location and a clean exit. Rafael walks into the exchange at a Danube warehouse, wearing a wire Elena's journalist contact is recording. Emotional beat: walking calmly toward the worst version of himself.

chapters.title: Everything Burns
chapters.summary: Climax part two, multi-POV. The wire is discovered; the warehouse erupts. Elena arrives with the one honest marshal left, Ilse uses the hostages' confusion to destroy the syndicate's local network files, and Rafael chooses saving Ilse over chasing his ex-wife's captor. The recording transmits. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the only clean currency left.

chapters.title: Testimony Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Aftermath, Rafael's POV. The summit leaks the ledgers; arrests ripple through the syndicate and the program. But Rafael, Elena, and Ilse are now fugitives too — their methods indictable, their protections void. In a safe flat in Ljubljana they watch the news name them persons of interest. Emotional beat: victory that costs citizenship in ordinary life.

chapters.title: Oscar
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Reveal: 'Oscar' was the codename his wife gave him during the trial — the ghost he became. He lets the name go, burns the last copy of his old identity, and chooses the two people beside him over the life he lost. Emotional beat: mourning finished, identity rebuilt from choice rather than fear.

chapters.title: The House with No Photos
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Elena's POV, six months later. The trio runs a small private service locating disappeared witnesses — justice outside the law, on their terms. A new client arrives with a listing photo of a house that shouldn't exist. Rafael smiles, packs the go-bag out of habit, and leaves it behind. Emotional beat: cautious hope; the cycle continues, but this time they hold the keys.
